ruxen 0.1.2: real-world nginx configurations load more often, static musl and ARM64 binaries, and a performance report against nginx on 83 scenarios. ruxen is an experimental nginx-compatible HTTP server and reverse proxy written from scratch in Rust: Linux-only, HTTP/1.1, thread-per-core on `io_uring` (monoio), TLS via rustls.

> [!WARNING]
> This is an experimental release. It is not production-ready and is not a drop-in replacement for nginx.

Where ruxen is going and in what order: [`ROADMAP.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/main/ROADMAP.md). The short version: an edge server (TLS termination, reverse proxy, static files) that loads nginx configurations as they are.

## Security

- **Low: [GHSA-5w2g-xpr2-gh39](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/security/advisories/GHSA-5w2g-xpr2-gh39).** `proxy_cookie_flags` was accepted and ignored, so upstream cookies reached clients without the `Secure`, `HttpOnly` or `SameSite` flags the configuration asked for. 0.1.0 and 0.1.1 are affected. ruxen can't apply the flags yet, so the directive is now refused at startup (`[emerg]`); `proxy_cookie_flags off;` still loads.

**Behaviour change:** configurations with `proxy_cookie_flags` (other than `off`) no longer start. Set the flags in the upstream application until ruxen implements the directive.

## Install

Three prebuilt binaries, each also under a versioned name (`ruxen-v0.1.2-<target>.tar.gz`), with a `SHA256SUMS` file:

| tarball | for |
| --- | --- |
| `ruxen-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz` | x86_64 with glibc 2.35 or newer |
| `ruxen-aarch64-linux-gnu.tar.gz` | ARM64 with glibc 2.35 or newer (Graviton, Ampere, Raspberry Pi 5 on a 64-bit OS) **(new)** |
| `ruxen-x86_64-linux-musl.tar.gz` | any x86_64 Linux, static (Alpine, older glibc) **(new)** |

```bash
curl -LO https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/releases/download/v0.1.2/ruxen-v0.1.2-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS   # after downloading SHA256SUMS from this release
tar xzf ruxen-v0.1.2-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz
cd ruxen-v0.1.2-x86_64-linux-gnu
./ruxen -t -c "$PWD/examples/minimal.conf"
```

`releases/latest/download/ruxen-<target>.tar.gz` always gets the newest release.

**The musl build** links mimalloc instead of musl's own allocator, which is slow under ruxen's many threads. Measured against the glibc build on the same machine (12 interleaved pairs): `proxy_hello` 97.3%, `tls_hello` 98.6%, `m1_hello` 98.0%. With musl's allocator it was 34.3%, 73.5% and 97.0%. The glibc builds keep the system allocator: mimalloc made `proxy_hello` 1.5% slower there.

From crates.io (needs `cmake` and a C compiler for rustls's `aws-lc-rs` backend):

```bash
cargo install ruxen --locked
```

Requirements: a Linux kernel with `io_uring` enabled. In Docker, run with `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined`: the default seccomp profile blocks `io_uring`.

## What's new since 0.1.1

### Real-world configurations

ruxen now measures how many real nginx configurations it loads: a corpus of application docs (Nextcloud, GitLab, Mastodon, Sentry, h5bp, …) and a few hundred public configurations, checked with `ruxen -t` against a current nginx as the control ([`corpus/RESULTS.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/v0.1.2/corpus/RESULTS.md)). **ruxen 0.1.2 loads 149 of the 238 configurations nginx accepts (63%); 0.1.1 loaded 113 (47%).** The fixes that came out of it:

- `proxy_*` directives at `http` level, inherited by servers and locations;
- a `server` without `listen` listens on `*:80`, or `*:8000` when not run as root, as in nginx;
- every nginx time unit (`d`, `w`, `M`, `y`, and combined values like `1h30m`);
- `proxy_cache_bypass` and `proxy_no_cache` accepted as no-ops, as nginx does without `proxy_cache` (the WebSocket boilerplate `proxy_cache_bypass $http_upgrade;`);
- the FastCGI / uWSGI / SCGI temp paths and `open_log_file_cache` accepted as checked no-ops;
- `index`, `error_page` and `recursive_error_pages` at `http` level; repeated `index` lines append, as in nginx;
- `merge_slashes` at `http` level now applies (it was accepted and ignored).

### nginx compatibility

- **Static files:**
  - `disable_symlinks` (`on`, `if_not_owner`, `from=`), enforced atomically with `openat2`. Configurations with it start again (0.1.1 refused them, see GHSA-qxw8-jfcm-4qrj);
  - variables in `try_files` probes and fallback;
  - `$request_filename`, `$document_root`, `$realpath_root`.
- **Request processing:**
  - regex captures `$1`…`$9` in every value that takes variables;
  - `map` results cached per request, and `map … volatile`;
  - the `Host` header kept as sent (routing still uses a lowercase copy);
  - `$server_addr`;
  - 204 responses sent without a body or body headers;
  - the `client_max_body_size` 413 goes through the location's `error_page`;
  - `client_body_temp_path` at `server` and `location` level, with `levels`; request-body temp files are unlinked when created.
- **Reverse proxy:**
  - `X-Accel-Redirect` keeps the upstream's headers, and refuses unsafe URIs with 404;
  - a bodiless `X-Accel-Redirect` response keeps the upstream connection in the keep-alive pool, as in nginx: 6.7× faster on the benchmark (#245);
  - upstream connections count against `worker_connections`.
- **Connections and workers:**
  - `listen` socket options reach the socket (`backlog`, `rcvbuf`, `sndbuf`, `deferred`, `fastopen`, `so_keepalive`, `ipv6only`);
  - `worker_shutdown_timeout`;
  - `worker_rlimit_nofile`, `worker_rlimit_core`;
  - `$proxy_protocol_tlv_*`.
- **TLS:**
  - certificates selected by SNI for regex and trailing-wildcard `server_name`s;
  - the handshake is bounded by `client_header_timeout`;
  - `BEGIN TRUSTED CERTIFICATE` blocks in `ssl_certificate`;
  - `$ssl_session_id`;
  - a TLS 1.2 renegotiation attempt is refused at once, and a TLS 1.3 KeyUpdate answered: both used to hang until a timeout.

**Behaviour change:** `listen [::]:80;` alone no longer serves IPv4 clients. The IPv6 socket is now `IPV6_V6ONLY` unless `ipv6only=off`, as in nginx, so the usual pair `listen 80; listen [::]:80;` binds two independent sockets.

The full list is the merged pull requests between `v0.1.1` and `v0.1.2`.

### Compatibility

ruxen is checked against the upstream [nginx-tests](https://github.com/nginx/nginx-tests) suite: **65 of the 106 test files** that ruxen opts into pass end-to-end (0.1.1: 63 of 105). The other 399 files are skipped because `ruxen -V` only claims the modules ruxen implements. Per-file status: [`NGINX_TEST_PROGRESS.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/v0.1.2/NGINX_TEST_PROGRESS.md).

## Performance

0.1.1 was about 1% slower than 0.1.0 on `proxy_hello` ([#177](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/issues/177)). On a quiet machine the loss turned out larger, about 4.6%, and a bisection put 3% of it on the client timeouts added in 0.1.1: every read and write re-armed the connection's timer. The timer is now armed only when an operation has to wait and moved about once a second. That recovered about 2%: 0.1.2 is at **96.9% of 0.1.0** on `proxy_hello` (12 interleaved pairs, 95.8–97.8%), and still above nginx on this scenario (111.2% on the i7, 96.2% on the i9 with ruxen as its own backend; 106–107% in front of a separate nginx backend). The rest stays open in #177.

For this release, ruxen was compared with nginx 1.24 on **83 scenarios** on two machines. Both servers load the same configuration file, and only paths both support are measured. Each ratio is the geometric mean of 8 interleaved A/B pairs (`bench/scripts/pair.sh`), `wrk -t16 -c512` unless noted, client and server on the same machine over loopback. The full report, with every scenario, latencies, calibration and caveats, is [`bench/campaign-0.1.2/REPORT.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/v0.1.2/bench/campaign-0.1.2/REPORT.md).

| | i7-9750H (6 cores, dedicated bench machine) | i9-13900HX (24 cores) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| scenarios where ruxen ≥ nginx | 60 of 83 | 26 of 83 |
| scenarios at ≥ 95% of nginx (the performance contract) | 64 of 83 | 54 of 83 |
| median ruxen / nginx | 109.4% | 96.9% |
| noise floor (ruxen vs a copy of itself) | ±1–2% | ±1–2% |

Selected scenarios (ruxen / nginx). The campaign measured the release candidate before #245 was fixed; the `X-Accel-Redirect` row is the fixed build, measured the same way (the other rows don't change: `proxy_hello` 100.1%, `proxy_ext_hello` 100.4% against the unfixed build).

| scenario | i7-9750H | i9-13900HX |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `return 200`, keep-alive (`m1_hello`) | 113.4% | 99.3% |
| `return 200`, no keep-alive (`m1_no_keepalive`) | 93.4% | 94.4% |
| static 1 KiB (`m3_static_1k`) | 132.5% | 103.2% |
| static 64 KiB (`static_64k`) | 104.6% | 99.2% |
| static 1 MiB (`m19_stream_1m`) | 64.5% | 101.2% |
| 304, `If-None-Match` (`m5_conditional_304`) | 117.7% | 96.2% |
| `try_files` SPA fallback (`try_files_fallback`) | 132.8% | 103.8% |
| `auth_basic` (`auth_basic_hello`) | 141.7% | 105.4% |
| `map` (`vars_map`) | 115.9% | 96.0% |
| 50 regex locations (`regex_locations_50`) | 106.2% | 67.9% |
| static 1 KiB + access log (`access_log_static_1k`) | 129.9% | 98.6% |
| reverse proxy, small response (`proxy_ext_hello`) | 106.4% | 107.4% |
| reverse proxy, no upstream keep-alive (`proxy_ext_no_keepalive`) | 108.9% | 109.5% |
| reverse proxy, 1 MiB response (`proxy_ext_1m`) | 35.8% | 55.1% |
| reverse proxy, 64 KiB POST (`proxy_ext_post_64k`) | 55.4% | 93.7% |
| reverse proxy, `X-Accel-Redirect` (`proxy_ext_xar`) | 105.3% | not re-measured (7.1% before the fix) |
| TLS 1.3, keep-alive (`tls_hello`) | 135.0% | 109.6% |
| TLS 1.3, a handshake per request (`tls13_handshake`) | 125.1% | 104.0% |
| TLS termination + proxy (`tls_proxy_hello`) | 120.0% | 102.2% |
| TLS 1.3, static 1 MiB (`tls_static_1m`) | 50.9% | 95.3% |

Where ruxen is clearly behind, each case has an issue:
- request bodies over 2 KiB are written to a temp file (#246);
- proxied responses are buffered whole (#88);
- 1 MiB responses at high concurrency on small machines (#247);
- regex matching cost on the larger machine (#248);
- autoindex (#250);
- new connections per request (#128) and many idle connections (#127).

Compared directly with 0.1.1 (same method), 0.1.2 is within noise on `m1_hello`, `proxy_hello`, `tls_hello`, `static_8k` and `m19_stream_1m` on both machines (99.8–101.3%).

## Known limitations

- `include` does not expand globs (`include conf.d/*.conf;`).
- Symlinks that lead outside `root` / `alias` are never followed (403), even with `disable_symlinks off`, where nginx serves them (`html/phpmyadmin -> /usr/share/phpmyadmin`).
- http-level `root`, `keepalive_*` and TLS defaults written below a `server` block don't apply to it ([#242](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/issues/242)); put them above the servers.
- A request that matches none of a server's locations gets 404; nginx serves it with the server-level settings, such as `root` ([#244](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/issues/244)). Add a `location /`.
- `if ($var = "")` and `!= ""` are refused at startup ([#243](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/issues/243)); `if ($var)` works where "0" may count as empty too.
- No HTTP/2 yet ([#144](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/issues/144)).
- Proxied responses are buffered whole before they are sent (up to 64 MiB); streaming them is planned, and so is WebSocket proxying.
- No configuration reload: `-s reload` is refused, restart instead.
- No epoll fallback: where `io_uring` is blocked (Docker's default seccomp profile, some Kubernetes and cloud setups), ruxen doesn't start.
- With `sendfile on`, the file side of the transfer is synchronous; `sendfile_max_chunk` is not configurable.
- `-V` reports `nginx version: nginx/1.29.2` (followed by `ruxen version: ruxen/0.1.2`): the nginx-tests harness reads that line and the `configure arguments` to decide which tests apply.

## How to help

- Found a config where nginx and ruxen behave differently, or one that ruxen refuses? Open an issue with the config, the request and both responses.
- Security problems: please report them privately, see [`SECURITY.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
- Setup, tests and benchmarks: [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
